newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-ADAMS MAKES EAGERLY AWAITED RETURN TO W.P..
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ADAMS MAKES EAGERLY AWAITED RETURN TO W.P..

text.p: South Africa's spin wizard Paul Adams makes his eagerly awaited return to first class action with a new weapon.
He will play for Western Province in their Supersport Series match against Boland at Newlands on Thursday, hoping to win a recall to the national side with a new angle of attack.
"I've been working on bowling over the wicket," Adams told Reuters. "It adds a new weapon to my armoury."

The left-arm wrist spinner has previously bowled around the wicket but the new line should enable him to win more lbw decisions with the googly, his stock delivery, which turns in to the right-handed batsman.
"I have been working on it in the nets since April and I have tried it in a couple of matches," he said. "But it's different bowling in the nets or a club match to a proper game."

The 19-year-old has not played a first class match since the beginning of August when shin splints and a groin problem forced him to sit out the remainder of the South Africa A team's tour of England and Wales.

Also returning to the Western Province side is Jacques Kallis although the all-rounder has been told he cannot bowl or field on the boundary. He recently suffered a recurrence of a back injury which forced him out of the A team's close season tour but is now deemed fit enough to play as a batsman.

Former test strike bowler Brett Schultz continues his comeback from injury in the Western Province B side. After making his debut for the province in their win over Northern Transvaal in the first round of Supersport Series matches he has been rested for the Boland match.

Boland, who lead the Supersport Series log from Western Province after winning their first match, hope to have strengthened their batting with the recall of Wayne Truter at number three and of all-rounder Billy Stelling for injured seamer Charl Willoughby, provided Stelling overcomes a rib injury.
Last season's runners-up Transvaal begin their campaign at newcomers Griqualand West by giving a debut to talented Mark Benfield.
The 19-year-old opener fills the gap left by the departure of Brad White to Border and he will partner Adam Bacher at the top of the innings.
Ross Veenstra, the former Natal all-rounder, also makes his official debut for Transvaal but there is no place for Richard Snell who is still recovering from a side strain.

New Northern Transvaal skipper Mark Davis plays his first game in the role in their home game with Free State after recovering from a rib injury which saw former West Indian skipper Richie Richardson lead the side against Western Province.

Davis replaces Nico Martin in the side with either Pierre Joubert or Deon Kruiswill coming in for pace bowler Greg Smith who has a groin injury. Free State have named two players without any 'A' section experience in their 13, in Kleinboet van Rensburg and Henk Botha.

Northern Transvaal have also announced the retirement of fast bowler Chris van Noordwyk because of a recurring back injury. He is joining the province's cricket academy as a coach under Anton Ferreira.

Border, who scored 385 in the fourth innings to beat Natal by four wickets in the opening round, include Peter Emslie for Brendan Horan in an otherwise unchanged 12 for the home derby with Eastern Province.
